description:
FOUND s491 (Fable, 2026-09-19) by a review probe written for perf round 34 (the overload-cache probes); PRE-EXISTING on main 4c6565e5, not caused by any open batch.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3): ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/povl-method.pl (+ .perl.out / .main-4c6565e5.out)
  package P; use overload "+" => "add", q("") => sub { "P" }; sub new { bless {}, shift } sub add { "added" }
  package C; our @ISA = ("P");  package main;  my $p = P->new; my $c = C->new;
  overload::Overloaded($p), ("C"), (bless {}, "Plain")  -> perl 1 1 0 ; PCL 1 0 0   (the CLASS-NAME STRING spelling misses inheritance; the object spelling is right since DECIDED "overload::Overloaded is inheritance-aware")
  my $m = overload::Method($p, "+"); ref($m), $m->($p,1,"")  -> perl CODE added ; PCL DIES: Undefined subroutine &OVERLOAD::Method called
  overload::Method($c, q(""))->($c) -> perl P (inherited) ; overload::Method($p, "-") and overload::Method("Plain", "+") -> undef

WHAT perl DOES: overload::Method(obj_or_class, op) returns the CODE ref that implements op for that class, walking @ISA; a by-NAME handler ("+" => "add") is returned as the resolved method (perl resolves it through the MRO at lookup); undef when there is none.  StrVal works in PCL today; Overloaded works for objects.

LAYER (CLAUDE.md 9a): `overload` is CORE and PCL provides it from the runtime (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~3688-3770: %p-overload-import / p-overloaded / StrVal live in the OVERLOAD package), so Method belongs beside them, reading the SAME per-class handler table through the SAME inheritance walk p-overloaded uses (`%p-class-overloaded-p`) -- one resolver, not a second walk (rule 11).  The class-name-string half of Overloaded is the same resolver given a string instead of a blessed box.

WHO USES IT: Test::Builder::_unoverload, Type::Tiny, Data::Printer, JSON::PP (`overload::Method($obj, q(""))` probes), Scalar::Util-style "is it stringifiable" idioms -- it is the standard way to ask "can this object do op".  Expect CPAN-board rows behind it (grep the board logs for "OVERLOAD::Method").

BAR: `cl/` runtime change -> full sweep + the op/ companion leg (op/overload*.t, lib/overload.t is not in the population); guard rows in Pl/t/overload-01.t (Method: own / inherited / by-name / absent / plain class; Overloaded on a class-name string).  If perf round 34 (s473x) ships a per-class overload CACHE, Method must read through it or be invalidated with it -- say which in ir-spec.

=== DONE (s491a) ===

SHIPPED.  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp only -- NO compiler change and NO emission
change: overload::Method reaches the runtime through the SAME seam as
overload::import, the OVERLOAD package, so `(overload::pl-Method $x "+")` --
which codegen already emitted, and which died "Undefined subroutine
&OVERLOAD::Method called" -- now resolves.  The symbol is interned MIXED CASE
(`pl-Method`) because `:invert` leaves a mixed-case token alone.

Guard: one row in Pl/t/overload-01.t (46 rows, 4.6 s wall), 18 assertions
inside it against a live perl run, FAILING on an extraction of 337f6a23.

ONE RESOLVER (rule 11): the direct `*p-overload-table*` entry then
%p-find-overload-mro -- the same two steps p-find-overload takes for the
operator dispatch.  The invocant is resolved by %pcl-invocant-class, the one
p-method-call / p-can / p-isa already share, which is what gives Overloaded
its class-name spelling for free.

PERL-PROBED, every row (scratch/s491a/probes/p1914.{pl,perl.out,s491a.out},
15 rows, IDENTICAL after the fix; the brief's own povl-method.pl too):

  overload::Overloaded          perl   PCL before   PCL after
  object of an overloading cls  1      1            1
  object of a SUBCLASS          1      1            1
  "P" (class-name string)       1      0            1     <- the second half
  "C" (subclass string)         1      0            1        of the bug
  "D" (grandchild string)       1      0            1
  "Plain" / unknown class       0      0            0
  an unblessed [] / ""          0      0            0
  a FALSE answer is UNDEF       undef  undef        undef

  overload::Method(X, op)       perl        PCL before   PCL after
  own code-ref handler          CODE        DIED         CODE
  inherited handler             CODE        DIED         CODE
  by-NAME handler ('+'=>'add')  CODE/added  DIED         CODE/added
  by-NAME, subclass OVERRIDES   CODE/       DIED         CODE/
    the named method            D-added                  D-added
  absent op                     undef       DIED         undef
  non-overloading class         undef       DIED         undef
  class-NAME string invocant    CODE        DIED         CODE
  'nomethod'                    CODE        DIED         CODE
  'fallback'                    undef       DIED         undef
  [] / undef / "" invocant      undef       DIED         undef

THE SHARP ONE is the by-name/subclass row: perl's ov_method does
`shift->can($name)`, so the handler NAME registered by the parent resolves
through the INVOCANT'S OWN MRO at LOOKUP TIME.  PCL answers it through
%p-can-answer -- member 3's returner -- which is also why a miss is perl's
undef and not CL NIL.

`fallback` answers undef for free: PCL keeps it in *p-overload-fallback*,
its own table, because it is not a handler, and perl agrees.  #1915 (the
fallback-die) is a DIFFERENT open bug; povl-fallback.pl still shows it and it
was not touched.
subject: `overload::Method` does not exist (dies "Undefined subroutine &OVERLOAD::Method called"), and `overload::Overloaded("ClassName")` answers 0 for a class that INHERITS its overloads -- the overload:: introspection family is two of four
